title: Design the scene IR: declarative Elixir scene graph + diff/patch semantics
description: The Elixir-side data model: entities (model/camera/light/environment/group), transforms, material parameter overrides, ids, pick handlers. Must align with mob's render/patch direction (scene tree in assigns, diffed, patches over the NIF wire — not full-tree resends). Decide coordinate conventions (document handedness + units ONCE, per the parity rule), what is per-frame vs structural, and the wire encoding. Deliverable: decision record in decisions/ + typespecs; no rendering required. Can run parallel to the spike.
notes: Design landed on branch design/scene-ir (aec08a6). Deliverables: decisions/2026-08-30-scene-ir.md (entity model, RH Y-up meters TRS, structural-vs-per-frame split, atomic canonical-order patch grammar riding Mob.Sender commits, declarative animation state w/ {:animation_done, play_id}, error taxonomy, caps-based version-skew per mob #111, applied-scene readback contract, IR->Filament mapping table for nhf); Mob.Scene3d.IR (structs+validate/1) + Mob.Scene3d.IR.Patch (pure diff/apply reference applier); property tests lock apply(a, diff(a,b)) == b. All gates green (format/credo --strict incl ExSlop/compile -Werror/40 tests). NOTE: this branch also created the mix scaffold (mix.exs, .credo.exs mirroring mob + ExSlop bundle enabled, .formatter.exs w/ stream_data) — spike lane had not pushed one; spike/filament-embed should rebase on design/scene-ir to pick it up. Open questions for owner in the decision doc's Consequences: pick-event tag shape vs Mob.UI {pid, tag} convention; Mob.Test alias for scene/1; asset-ref root ownership (392).

title: Spike: embed Filament on both platforms and render a .glb into a Mob surface
description: De-risk the prebuilt-binary link step before any API design commits: link Filament's Android AAR into the Gradle build and the iOS xcframework into the xcode/zig build, create an engine+swapchain against a CAMetalLayer (iOS) and SurfaceView (Android) hosted inside a Mob screen, load one .glb via gltfio, render with a directional light and IBL. Acceptance: same asset visibly identical on one physical Android + one iOS device/sim; binary-size delta recorded; exact Filament version pinned; build-time delta recorded. Everything else in the DAG assumes this spike's answers.
notes:
Spike in progress on branch spike/filament-embed (worktree /Users/kevin/code/worktrees/s3d-spike). Pinned Filament v1.75.1 — newest version on BOTH GitHub releases (iOS tgz) and Maven Central (Android AARs); v1.76.0 (2026-08-28) exists on GitHub but AARs not on Maven yet, and mob_dev's plugin gradle_deps mechanism is Maven-Central-only. Findings so far: (1) iOS release artifacts ARE xcframeworks (32 of them, static libs) incl. libgltfio_core, libktxreader, libbasis_transcoder, libuberarchive — gltfio+KTX2 included, device+sim slices; (2) Android AARs (filament/gltfio/filament-utils 1.75.1) all 16KB page-aligned arm64 .so; (3) filament-utils AAR is Java-17 bytecode → generated app template's jvmTarget 1.8 must be bumped to 17; (4) no .xcodeproj in mob apps — ios/build.zig edits needed: ObjC++ compile step (xcrun cc, gnu++17), bridging-header wrap, link ~20 static archives + Metal framework. Baselines: iOS binary 7,982,664 B (.app 8.3MB, deploy 3m30s); Android APK 77,553,781 B (deploy 3m15s).
Coordinator extended the Android evidence to PHYSICAL hardware: spike APK + full --native deploy on the Moto g power (Android 11, arm64), Filament 1.75.1 rendering bevel_cube.glb in the Mob screen, navigated via Mob.Test.tap(:open_scene3d) over distribution (screen/1 confirmed HomeScreen→Scene3dScreen). Owner eyeballed it live. Deploy potholes recorded upstream as mob_dev issue (non-native deploy reports success without the OTP runtime). Android half of the spike is DONE on emulator + physical; iOS remains.
Both platforms rendering+spinning. Deltas: Android APK +11,661,536 B (3 ABIs); iOS sim binary +3,359,360 B (dead_strip). Two bugs found+fixed during verify: (a) ModelViewer.transformToUnitCube centers model at (0,0,-4) so spin must compose base*rotation not rotation*base (model orbited out of frame); (b) Metal-on-SIMULATOR shadow pass zeroes direct light -> fully black model with correct silhouette; setShadowingEnabled(false) fixes; Android GLES shadows fine. Also: Mob.Test.screenshot returns view-hierarchy WITHOUT SurfaceView contents (byte-identical PNGs while animating) — 3D evidence needs adb screencap/simctl io. Gradle PKIX failure behind Cloudflare WARP fixed via custom truststore. Remaining: physical Moto acceptance (waiting on lease, frees ~18:25).
Both platforms rendering+spinning. Deltas: Android APK +11.66MB (3 ABIs); iOS sim binary +3.36MB (dead_strip). Bugs found+fixed during verify: (a) ModelViewer.transformToUnitCube centers model at (0,0,-4) so spin must compose base*rotation not rotation*base; (b) Metal-on-SIMULATOR shadow pass zeroes direct light -> black model; setShadowingEnabled(false) fixes; Android GLES shadows fine. Mob.Test.screenshot omits SurfaceView contents — 3D evidence needs adb screencap / simctl io screenshot. Gradle PKIX behind Cloudflare WARP fixed via custom JVM truststore. Remaining: physical Moto acceptance.
SPIKE COMPLETE — deliverables on branch spike/filament-embed (HEAD e60e8cd, pushed). Verdict: feasible-with-caveats; full Q&A in decisions/2026-08-30-filament-spike.md. Verified rendered+spinning .glb on physical Moto ZY22DP6HFL + pool iOS sim (+ pool emulator); evidence/ has screenshots+videos; app uninstalled everywhere, all leases released. NOTE: bd close refused — DAG lists b9g as blocked by t05/nhf/392, which is inverted (those beads consume this spike's answers); left IN_PROGRESS rather than --force. Human should flip the dependency direction and close.

title: Name-scoped material override: tint one named glTF material, not the whole instance
description: Gap found by chopaat asset round 3 (chopaat-xix, two-tone pawns). The IR Material override (Model.material / set_material) is per-entity: the native appliers loop EVERY materialInstance of the gltfio instance (MobScene3dBridge.kt applyMaterial: `for (mi in instance.materialInstances)`), so a base_color override repaints all materials of the model. chopaat's round-3 pawn ships TWO named materials — pawn_body (player-tintable) and pawn_accent (authored ivory that must NOT take the tint) — so the driving consumer needs a name-scoped override, e.g. Model.materials: %{"pawn_body" => %Material{...}} (or a Material.target field), with native filtering materialInstances by glTF material name (Filament MaterialInstance.name carries it). Grammar extension per the version-skew rules: new field + caps bump, never silently-ignored keys. Reproduction: chopaat feat/assets-round3 priv/assets/pawn.glb + Chopaat.Scene.pawn_entities/6 tint path — the ivory collar/tip take the player color. Consumer-side follow-up tracked on chopaat-xix (scope pawn tint + selected emissive + target markers to pawn_body).
notes: CORRECTION: final HEAD is b563dc7 (amended — the earlier 36054fa push was missing the iOS texture-provider fix + iOS evidence due to a commit-hook interruption; branch force-pushed with lease). Verified HEAD contains MobScene3dView.mm texture providers, CHANGELOG Fixed entry, and all 6 evidence files.

title: Environment/IBL loading in the applier: wire cmgen KTX into IndirectLight + Skybox
description: The applier accepts Environment entities but logs-and-ignores (honest stub from plugin core). Wire it: load the cmgen-produced _ibl.ktx (prefiltered specular + SH) and _skybox.ktx from priv scene3d assets via ktxreader (already in the prebuilts), build IndirectLight + Skybox per the Filament mapping table, both platforms. The asset pipeline half (mix scene3d.assets --ibl) is done and verified. Acceptance: a PBR model under IBL-only lighting renders with visibly correct reflections on device; environment swap via replace patch works; readback exposes the applied env refs. Sim shadows caveat does not apply (IBL has no shadow pass).

title: Android ui_components codegen: plugin manifest declares the viewport composable but nothing registers it in the host MainActivity
description: Reproduction (chopaat-mgw, 2026-08-30): a fresh mob.adopt.native host app with mob_scene3d activated (mob.exs plugins + manifest nifs wired, MobScene3dBridge.kt compiled in, MobPluginBootstrap.registerAll generated and called) renders a Mob.Scene3d.viewport/1 node as NOTHING — MobNativeViewRegistry.render returns silently because no factory is registered under 'Mob_Scene3d_Viewport'. Device evidence: chopaat android emulator (buildpool2) — Elixir side fully healthy (Mob.Scene3d.Viewport ComponentServer alive, handle 0, 27 entities committed, caps schema 1 ok) yet Mob.Scene3d.viewports/1 == [] and the screenshot shows no viewport (chopaat evidence/android_emu_game_t0.png). The manifest's ui_components entry (android: composable MobScene3dViewport) is data nobody consumes on Android: s3d_spike registers the composable BY HAND in MainActivity.kt:159, and every adopting host must copy that. Fix: mob_dev plugin codegen (MobPluginBootstrap) should emit MobNativeViewRegistry.register entries from the manifest's ui_components, or the bridge's register() should do it (needs access to the app-package MobNativeViewRegistry — the reason it can't today). Silent-return on missing factory is also a phantom-ok per AGENTS: consider logging a loud error. Workaround in chopaat MainActivity carries this bead id.
notes: FIX IMPLEMENTED — PR: https://github.com/GenericJam/mob_dev/pull/56 (awaiting coordinator review; not merged). Owning repo: mob_dev (NativeBuild generates MobPluginBootstrap.kt each native build for both mob.new and mob.adopt hosts; IOSBootstrap was the working iOS analog). Mechanism: new MobDev.Plugin.AndroidBootstrap classifies ui_components and NativeBuild splices MobNativeViewRegistry.register calls into the generated registerAll(this) — key = android.view_module || ios.view_module, bare composable qualified with the bridge_class package, app package discovered from the file defining 'object MobNativeViewRegistry' and referenced fully qualified (the reason a plugin bridge's own register() never could). Loud failure: typo'd composable = Gradle compile error; malformed declaration = Mix.raise at build; non-identifier composable = validator error; declared-but-unresolvable (manual tier-2) = generated red 'Missing native component' tile + Log.e, overwritable by the host's later registration; registry-less hosts (LV wrapper) = printed build warning. Verified compile-level on a fresh mix mob.new host with mob_scene3d as path dep: registration emitted with NO hand edit; gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin green for registration + placeholder variants; typo'd composable fails compile as designed. No device run (pool hardware leased; deploy pointed at a nonexistent device id). Gates: format, credo --strict, compile --warnings-as-errors, full mix test (2180 passed), erlfmt — all green; security_scan --strict only flags 6 pre-existing ~/.mob/cache bundled-runtime drift findings present on master. chopaat-df3 noted with removal steps. Worktree: scratchpad/mob_dev-q03, branch fix/android-ui-components-bootstrap.

title: Cross-platform parity harness: same scene, both devices, sampled and compared
description: The plugin's core promise — identical output on both platforms — as a numeric regression gate, not a claim. Render a fixed probe scene (known materials, lights, IBL, one glb) on a leased iOS and Android device, sample_region a grid of probe points on each, compare within a stated tolerance (expect small tone-mapping/dither deltas; the tolerance IS the documented parity contract). Runs against every plugin change that touches the applier, materials, or Filament version. This is the acceptance instrument for the 'one design, two platforms' thesis applied to 3D; build it as soon as the applier renders (right after the spike + minimal applier), BEFORE feature work piles up.
notes:
Spike constraint: the parity harness cannot rely on Mob.Test.screenshot/sample_region over the 3D surface (SurfaceView blindspot — see 0n7 note). Use Filament readPixels GPU readback exposed via the introspection NIF as the sampling primitive — which is BETTER for parity anyway (pre-compositor, excludes OS chrome).
Sampler primitive MERGED (Mob.Scene3d.sample_region via readPixels). Parity findings the harness must encode: base_color {0.9,0.05,0.05} → dominant 0xFFCE3934 BYTE-IDENTICAL Moto vs iOS sim (post ACES/sRGB); emulator within 1/255/channel; Filament dithering keeps dominant_share at 0.30-0.48 on flat fills — assert dominance + per-channel tolerance bands, never share≈1.0 or bit-exact vs IR colors. Alpha normalized opaque at readback.

title: Agent introspection + Mob.Test integration (feature gate for everything)
description: Mob.Scene3d.pick(node, x, y) → entity-or-honest-error; Mob.Scene3d.scene(node) → applied scene graph as data (readback from the applier, not the Elixir-side intent — the point is detecting divergence); reuse Mob.Test.sample_region for pixel truth. Per AGENTS.md this is a merge gate: no rendering feature ships without its introspection counterpart. Includes docs in the testing guide.
notes:
Scope addition: performance must be introspectable too, or it becomes the one blind spot in an otherwise agent-legible stack — add frame-time readback (rolling avg/p95 frame ms, dropped-frame count since last query, entity/drawcall counts) to the introspection API so agents can assert 'renders at 60fps with 200 pieces on the low-end pool device' as a number, not a vibe. Filament exposes the timing; plumb it through the same NIF readback as scene/1.
CRITICAL spike finding for introspection: Mob.Test.screenshot CANNOT see SurfaceView content on Android (byte-identical PNGs while visibly animating — window capture excludes the SurfaceView layer). Compositor capture (adb screencap composites correctly) or GPU readback (Filament readPixels) is required for any pixel-truth path. sample_region/sample_color on the 3D region has the same blindspot risk — verify on both platforms and choose GPU readback if window capture fails. This also constrains the parity harness.
Mob.Test alias ruling could NOT land on Mob.Test: mob core has no plugin-extension mechanism for Mob.Test (closed module in the dep; a plugin cannot add functions to mob's namespace without monkey-patching the beam). Aliases shipped as Mob.Scene3d.Test.{scene/1,pick/3,sample_region/2,frame_stats/1,viewports/1} with identical node-first shapes. CANDIDATE MOB ISSUE: a Mob.Test plugin-extension seam (e.g. Mob.Test delegating unknown introspection calls to registered plugin modules, or a use-macro plugins adopt). When it lands, Mob.Scene3d.Test delegates unchanged. Also: sample_region reduces raw native RGBA through Mob.Test.reduce_rgba/3 (public+pure) so 2D/3D stats shapes are identical by construction.
iOS sim verification gap (documented, not hidden): tap->event on iOS could not be driven end-to-end — Mob.Test.tap_xy on SIMULATORS is accessibility-activation only (mob ios/mob_nif.m tap_xy(sim) path: 'simulator rejects in-process synthetic IOHIDEvents'; plain gesture recognizers have no AX action), and a CAMetalLayer view exposes no AX element, so tap_xy returns {:error,:no_element_at_point}. The pool's physical iPhone was ABSENT. What IS verified on the iOS sim: pick/3 hit+miss (the same pickAtPixelX path taps ride, coordinate mapping included), scene/1, sample_region (GPU readback), frame_stats (clean 16.667ms avg/p95, 0 dropped @60Hz). The touch->{tag,id}->screen delivery chain is verified end-to-end on Android emulator AND physical Moto via real input injection; the Elixir forwarding code is platform-shared. Residual untested iOS link: UITapGestureRecognizer firing on real hardware. Follow-up: re-verify when the iPhone is attached; candidate mob issue: simulator-grade touch injection for non-AX views.
Implemented + device-verified on branch feat/pick-introspect (HEAD 5cc973a). MEASURED SAMPLER VALUES (tone-mapping tolerance findings): IR base_color {0.9,0.05,0.05} probe under 110k-lux sun + sunny-16 exposure + ACES samples dominant 0xFFCE3934 on BOTH physical Moto and iOS sim (byte-identical!), pool emulator within 1/255 per channel; skybox {0.035,0.04,0.07} samples 0xFF262C43 on all three. Filament dithering keeps dominant_share at only ~0.30-0.48 even on flat fills — parity harness (zn8) must assert dominance/channel-ordering/tolerance bands, never dominant_share≈1.0 or bit-exact vs IR colors. Swap-chain alpha normalized to opaque at the readback boundary (GLES leaves it 0; surface composites opaque). FRAME_STATS: Moto rest avg 16.709/p95 16.789ms 0 dropped; under 120-frame per-frame move loop avg 16.707/p95 16.808ms 0 dropped 152 frames (sustained 60fps on hardware); iOS sim 16.667/16.667 0 dropped; redroid emulator honestly slow (~93-100ms avg). renderables count includes the skybox renderable (2 cubes + skybox = 3). scene/1 world transforms matched applied patches on all three targets.

title: Input + picking: touch → ray pick → {:pick, entity} events
description: Touch capture in the shims, ray-pick against the Filament scene in the applier, entity id delivered to the owning screen process as {:pick, id} (handle_info, matching mob's tap event grammar). Honest miss: no event OR a documented miss event — decide and document; no phantom picks. On-device acceptance on physical hardware both platforms.
notes:
Miss semantics ruled + documented (addendum in decisions/2026-08-30-scene-ir.md, details in decisions/2026-08-30-pick-introspection.md): tap resolving to nothing pickable = NO event (silence, like 2D dead space); hit on pickable:false model = same miss; pick/3 answers both with {:error,{:no_entity_at_point,x,y}}. Event grammar per post-review ruling: on_pick: tag on the viewport (default :pick), {tag, entity_id} to the owning screen's handle_info/2. Delivery is async-resolved (Filament GPU pick, a frame or two later). Coordinates: viewport-local dp/pt origin top-left at the API; shims scale+flip to GL bottom-left internally.
Implemented + device-verified on branch feat/pick-introspect (HEAD 5cc973a). Real-input tap acceptance: pool emulator AND physical Moto (ZY22DP6HFL) — adb input tap on the red pickable probe delivers {:probe_picked, "probe"} to the screen's handle_info; taps on the pickable:false decoy and on background leave :picks untouched (miss = silence). pick/3 hit+miss verified on emulator, iOS pool sim, and Moto. iOS real-touch verification deferred: sim tap synthesis is AX-only (can't reach a Metal view's gesture recognizer) and the pool iPhone was absent — the shared native pick path is verified on iOS via pick/3; gap noted on 0n7. Evidence: evidence/android_{emu,moto}_*, evidence/ios_sim_*. All AGENTS.md gates green; leases released, apps uninstalled.

title: Asset pipeline: .glb via gltfio, KTX2 textures, cmgen IBL, mix scene3d.assets task
description: glb-only ingestion (embedded buffers, single file per asset in priv/); KTX2/Basis for standalone textures; IBL environments precomputed with Filament cmgen (prefiltered specular + SH irradiance) shipped in priv/ and referenced by name. mix scene3d.assets wraps conversion/validation (reject loose .gltf, FBX, OBJ, USDZ with actionable messages naming the converter). Document the authoring workflow (Blender export settings) in a guide.
notes:
Scope addition: a conformance sweep over the Khronos glTF-Sample-Models corpus (or a curated subset) through gltfio ingestion, asserting load success + scene readback shape per model. Validates the asset path against the world's assets, not just our own Blender exports; failures become a known-unsupported list documented in the asset guide rather than surprises in consumers.
Landed on branch feat/scaffold-and-assets (PR #1). mix scene3d.assets: .glb-only (converter guidance names @gltf-transform/cli cp / FBX2glTF / obj2gltf / Blender; USDZ called out as Apple-only dead end), embedded-buffer rule, Khronos validation via gltf-transform validate (PATH or npx), gltfio supported-extension judgments (extensionsRequired outside the list = error, used-only = warning; list pinned to priv/filament-version, revisit on bumps), budgets from .scene3d_assets.exs (max_file_bytes/max_triangles/require_ktx2, unknown keys raise), --ktx2 etc1s|uastc (pre-checks KTX-Software's ktx binary — no brew formula, guidance points at releases; verified end-to-end with 4.4.2), --ibl via cmgen --deploy (vendored by scripts/fetch_cmgen.sh from the pinned Filament release; NOTE cmgen names outputs after the deploy DIR, so the dir name is the env name). Conformance sweep: scripts/fetch_gltf_samples.sh sparse-checkouts 20 curated Khronos sample models + derives Draco (gltf-transform draco) and KTX2 (repacked KTX-BasisU variant) coverage → 22/22 pass; EXT_meshopt_compression verified rejected. Table + authoring workflow in guides/assets.md. Boundary: sweep validates pipeline judgments only — gltfio runtime load/render acceptance needs the native applier + scene readback (plugin-core / Mob.Test lanes). Decision record: decisions/2026-08-30-asset-pipeline.md. Asset root stays priv/scene3d_assets/ per the scene-IR ruling.

title: Surface + lifecycle shims: CAMetalLayer/CADisplayLink and SurfaceView/Choreographer
description: Per-platform plumbing only: surface creation inside a Mob screen node, vsync-driven frame loop, resize, background/foreground pause-resume, teardown when the owning screen exits (register with mob's component-owner reclamation — precedent mob #111: cleanup must run before user terminate/2 and survive raising callbacks). No scene logic here.
notes:
Spike answers are merged (decisions/2026-08-30-filament-spike.md + s3d_spike/ reference code): Engine created ON the main thread, frames driven from Choreographer/CADisplayLink, 60fps sustained both platforms. jvmTarget 1.8→17 required (filament-utils AAR is Java-17 bytecode). Shadow pass BLACKS OUT the model on Metal simulator — gate shadows off when running on sim (physical renders fine). transformToUnitCube centers at (0,0,-4): compose base*rotation for spins.
Lifecycle plan: Android SurfaceView+UiHelper+Choreographer (attach->postFrameCallback, detach->remove+destroy renderer, shadow survives in bridge); iOS CAMetalLayer+CADisplayLink with UIApplicationDidEnterBackground/WillEnterForeground pause-resume, didMoveToWindow attach/detach, TARGET_OS_SIMULATOR compile-time shadows gate. iOS build wiring must be DEVICE-CAPABLE (coordinator scope add): build_device.zig gets the same Filament treatment with ios-arm64 slices, -miphoneos-version-min, device OTP includes; shadows ON for physical Metal (verify on hardware).
iOS sim acceptance PASSED (pool-ios-2): CADisplayLink loop, resize/projection, teardown on screen exit, re-attach shadow replay verified (t3 re-entered scene renders). Sim trap found: pool sims are BOOTED with a persistent SIMCTL_CHILD_MOB_SIM_RUNTIME_DIR pointing at a per-device dir that may not exist — override at launch (SIMCTL_CHILD_MOB_SIM_RUNTIME_DIR=$HOME/.mob/runtime/ios-sim) or populate it. Device-slice build (build_device.zig + ios-arm64 Filament slices) compiles, LINKS, and code-signs clean — physical install blocked only by the iPhone being unreachable/locked (devicectl 'unavailable', attach state flapping). Moto native deploy in flight.
Surface/lifecycle shims verified: Android SurfaceView+UiHelper+Choreographer with onWindowVisibilityChanged pause/resume + full engine teardown on detach; iOS CAMetalLayer+CADisplayLink with UIApplication background/foreground pause-resume, didMoveToWindow attach/detach, layoutSubviews resize/projection, dealloc teardown mirroring the spike; teardown rides Viewport.terminate/2 (mob #111) destroying the NIF-side shadow — re-enter rebuilds cleanly (proven all 3 targets). PHYSICAL IPHONE: device-slice build (build_device.zig + ios-arm64 Filament archives) compiles, links, and code-signs clean; shadows compile-time-gated only on TARGET_OS_SIMULATOR so the device binary has shadows ON; install blocked — iPhone SE paired but devicectl-unavailable (disconnected since 19:32), monitor armed, lease held (7200s).
PHYSICAL IPHONE disposition: install NOT completed. Device-slice binary (arm64, Filament ios-arm64 slices, shadows ON — TARGET_OS_SIMULATOR gate only) compiles, links, and code-signs clean; two devicectl install attempts failed with CoreDeviceError 4016 (cannot assert remoteServiceDiscoveryTrustedConnectivityAvailable). Phone IS on USB (idevice_id lists it, lockdown pairing validates, PasswordProtected=false) but CoreDevice has shown it 'unavailable' since 19:32 — needs a human replug/unlock; no sudo to kick remoted. Retry recipe once reconnected: pool phys lease iphone && cd s3d_spike && mix mob.deploy --native --device 00008110-001E1C3A34F8401E (build is warm, ~1 min). All leases released (moto, buildpool1, pool-ios sims, iphone); apps uninstalled from moto/emulator/sim.
PHYSICAL IPHONE VERIFIED (2026-08-31): device-slice build (ios-arm64 Filament archives, shadows ON) deployed via mob.deploy --native after the owner reconnected the phone (CoreDevice 4016 cleared by replug/unlock as predicted). App installed, running, owner confirmed rendering live ('Working!'). Note: host-side dist connect via mob.connect returned no nodes on first try — physical-iOS dist tunneling is the known finicky area (app-ii3 family); tap-by-intent driving on physical iOS remains to be exercised in chopaat-4nn. The plugin core is now proven on all four targets: emulator, iOS sim, physical Android, physical iOS.

title: NIF wire + native scene applier (IR patches → Filament scene, both platforms)
description: Shared C++ applier translating IR patches into Filament entity/component mutations, exposed via NIF on both platforms; structural changes (add/remove entities, asset refs) and per-frame changes (transforms, material params) handled distinctly. Honest errors for unknown ids/bad patches — never silent no-ops. Host tests for the patch protocol; on-device test renders + mutates a scene and reads it back.
notes:
IR design is MERGED to master (decisions/2026-08-30-scene-ir.md + lib/mob/scene3d/ir.ex + ir/patch.ex, 40 tests incl. round-trip property). The applier lane implements from the Filament mapping table at the bottom of the decision doc. Post-review rulings included: on_pick configurable tag delivering {tag, entity_id}; Mob.Test.scene/1 + pick/3 aliases; patches are atomic reject-all riding the Sender commit path, diffed against last COMMITTED IR.
Threading contract from the spike (HARD): BEAM schedulers must NEVER call Filament — the NIF enqueues IR patches to the render thread (Filament API is single-threaded on the Engine-creating thread; internal driver thread handles GPU submission). Apply patches between frames on the Choreographer/CADisplayLink tick. Spike reference code merged under s3d_spike/.
Design settled for plugin-core lane (feat/plugin-core): NIF = mob_camera-pattern plugin NIF (erl stub + .m on iOS, zig->Kotlin bridge on Android). scene3d_apply validates the WHOLE patch synchronously against a native SHADOW registry (pure bookkeeping, no Filament — safe on BEAM thread), returns result JSON; validated ops enqueue to the render thread (Choreographer/CADisplayLink) and apply between frames. Renderer is REBUILDABLE from the shadow on view (re)attach — solves both patches-before-attach and iOS navVersion root-reset (any push/pop transition rebuilds the SwiftUI tree and recreates the native view; makeUIView must re-attach + replay). Commit path: screen passes ir: %IR{} as native_view prop; only render/1 output rides the 2D JSON (verified: Mob.Component.expand replaces node props with render/1 result), so Viewport component's update/2 diffs vs last committed (held in component state) and ships the patch — same-paint synchronous, serialized per viewport by the component process. Teardown rides mob #111 component reclamation (terminate/2 -> scene3d_destroy). Animation ops honestly unsupported (set_animation absent from native caps; add/replace with animation != nil errors [unsupported,animation]). Environment accepted-but-logged (KTX/IBL is bead 392). Wire: versioned JSON envelope, lib/mob/scene3d/wire.ex, fixed error-atom whitelists.
Android emulator acceptance PASSED end-to-end (buildpool1 redroid13 x86_64): add/move/remove/honest-errors/teardown/re-enter all verified over distribution; evidence in evidence/android_emu_plugin_*.png. Two wire bugs found+fixed on device: org.json optString(null)=='null' string (parent refs), and on-device BEAM ignores config.exs app env (asset_root now set at app start). iOS sim build in progress.
PLUGIN CORE LANDED on feat/plugin-core (through 056e952, pushed). Verification matrix: Android emulator (buildpool1 redroid13 x86_64) PASS, iOS pool sim (pool-ios-2) PASS, physical Moto (ZY22DP6HFL) PASS incl. motion screenrecord — full acceptance drive each: bootstrap render of chopaat probe.glb, 20-step per-frame move with world-transform readback agreement, remove->gone, unknown-id + duplicate-add -> synchronous taxonomy errors, screen exit -> teardown (post-exit readback errors honestly), re-enter -> scene rebuilt from shadow. Evidence: evidence/{android_emu,ios_sim,android_moto}_plugin_*. HONEST STUBS: (1) animation — set_animation absent from native caps (Elixir guard refuses loudly); add/replace_entity with a non-nil animation rejects [unsupported,animation] at the native shadow (defense in depth; Elixir caps guard checks op NAMES only). (2) Environment accepted-but-logged; KTX/IBL is bead 392. (3) pickable maintained in registry only; picking is bead na8. (4) set_material nil restores asset-authored factors by instance rebuild; overridden instances are never reused (gltfio has no per-instance destroy — bounded leak, documented in code). (5) plugin unsigned — test app uses acknowledge_unsafe_plugins; sign at release. Wire schema 1; caps guard + schema mismatch host-tested. 76 host tests green; all gates green (format/credo --strict/warnings-as-errors/erlfmt/clang-format/ktlint/swiftlint; MainActivity has 62 PRE-EXISTING template ktlint findings, zero new).
Plugin core MERGED to master after independent verification (76 tests re-run, credo clean; device evidence reviewed on 3/4 targets). Physical iPhone install remains the only open line — blocked on CoreDevice 4016 (phone needs human replug/unlock; build warm, retry recipe in t05 notes). Downstream lanes unblocked: na8 picking and 0n7 introspection build against the merged applier + shadow registry.

title: Full-size screenrecord virtual display shows the scene3d SurfaceView black on redroid (regression vs earlier native)
description: Found from chopaat (bead chopaat-4g7 device evidence). On the redroid pool emulator (127.0.0.1:5821, redroid13_x86_64_only), 'adb shell screenrecord' at the native 1080x2340 size records the scene3d viewport as solid BLACK while the HUD renders fine. Repro: chopaat feat/camera-orbit, mix mob.deploy --native to 5821, run scripts/device_orbit_evidence.exs with CHOPAAT_RECORD=adb:127.0.0.1:5821 and no CHOPAAT_RECORD_SIZE. Evidence that this is a native-side regression, not a redroid constant: chopaat evidence/android_emu_turn_cycle.mp4 (recorded 2026-08-31 12:52, same emulator, same 1080x2340 full-size screenrecord) captured the viewport correctly with the previously-installed native; after rebuilding the APK from current mob_scene3d HEAD (the material_scope-capable native), the same full-size capture is black. screencap stills capture fine; scaled capture (screenrecord --size 540x1170) captures fine; physical Moto (ZY22DP6HFL) full-size capture fine. Suspect changed EGL/swapchain/surface usage flags in the Android view. Workaround in chopaat: CHOPAAT_RECORD_SIZE=540x1170 in scripts/device_orbit_evidence.exs (comment references this bead).

title: Release readiness: plugin distribution + 0.2.0 to Hex
description: mob_scene3d cannot ship as a normal hex plugin until iOS prebuilt static libs have a plugin-manifest slot (mob_dev issue #55) — hosts currently need the documented hand wiring (bridging header, .mm compile, fetch_filament_ios.sh, archives). This bead: (1) drive/land the mob_dev #55 manifest surface, (2) migrate the hand wiring into the manifest, (3) verify a FRESH mob.new host consumes mob_scene3d from a plain dep with zero hand edits on BOTH platforms, (4) decide the hex-publish moment with the owner (HEX_API_KEY is deliberately absent; adding it publishes on the next mix.exs push per release.yml), (5) sign the plugin (test apps currently use acknowledge_unsafe_plugins). This is the 'anyone can use it' gate.

title: Camera framing transitions + gesture-driven controls
description: Two halves: (1) smooth camera framing — eased transitions between camera states driven from the IR (a %CameraMove{} per-frame interpolation helper in Elixir, no native change: the camera is already patchable per frame), with framing presets (frame-entity, frame-all); (2) gesture capture beyond tap in the shims (drag, pinch) surfaced as viewport events so the existing 10j orbit/pan/zoom helpers have inputs. Folds bead mob_scene3d-10j's scope in — close 10j into this or implement both together. Device acceptance: orbit a scene by real drag on physical Android.

title: Skinned-mesh + morph-target animation through the runtime applier
description: The asset pipeline accepts rigged models (RiggedSimple, CesiumMan, Fox, morph tests pass conformance) but the applier's animation path has only been device-verified with TRS-track clips (tumbles). Verify gltfio Animator drives skinned + morph animations on both platforms through our set_animation surface; fix what breaks; add a rigged model to the device acceptance battery. Unlocks character-style content (the future gandi pawn could be rigged).

title: Light types: point + spot, multiple lights, documented intensity units
description: Directional works. Add point and spot (Filament LightManager supports all three; IR Light data already has a type field), multiple simultaneous lights, and DOCUMENT the intensity units per type (Filament uses lux for directional, lumens for point/spot — the cross-platform parity contract needs the units pinned). Per-light shadow toggle (castShadows) with the sim gate respected. Device acceptance via sample_region on lit vs unlit faces.

title: Per-instance texture overrides (skins) + verify alpha blend modes
description: Today material overrides are factor tints only. Add texture-swap capability: override a named material's baseColor texture on an instance (MaterialInstance setParameter with a Texture loaded from a KTX2/PNG asset ref) — the 'skin' system (e.g. alternate board cloths, pawn skins). Also verify gltfio alpha modes (OPAQUE/MASK/BLEND) render correctly through the applier — glass-ish UI in 3D depends on it. IR: extend the material override struct additively (texture refs), caps bump per versioning rules, honest unsupported on old natives. Consider the cheap fallback (asset variants) in the decision record and say when each applies.

title: IR surface for per-slot mesh substitution on an animated model instance (Chopaat slot-mesh)
description: Driving-consumer gap from chopaat-hre (integration bead). Chopaat's tumble entity is one Model instance of tumbles.glb: 7 slot nodes shell_0..shell_6 carrying a canonical proxy hull mesh, retargeted by 32 baked animations. The game wants its per-game cosmetic pool shells (e.g. cowrie_money_a.glb) to RIDE THE SLOTS during flight. Today the IR cannot express that: Model.asset is whole-instance and structural (a changed asset diffs to :replace_entity = destroy+recreate of the entire instance, tumbles animations included), and an Entity cannot parent to a *named glTF node* of another instance — parent references are entity ids only. So per-slot mesh assignment inside an animated instance has no surface. Repro: build Chopaat's game scene (chopaat repo, Chopaat.Scene.build/3 with a :throw_animation), try to show pool shell meshes tumbling — only the proxy hulls can play the clips. Wanted (either): (a) Model node_meshes: %{node_name => asset_ref} applied after instance load, or (b) entity attachment to a named node of another instance (parent: {entity_id, node_name}) so slot-riding meshes inherit animated transforms. Workaround in chopaat (v1, tagged with this bead id): proxy hulls perform the flight, real pool shells pose at rest after settle; removal tracked by the chopaat bead created alongside this one.

title: Docs + example app (the catalog for 3D)
description: Guides: getting started, asset authoring, scene IR reference, agent driving (pick/scene/sample recipes). Example app doubling as the visual catalog: one screen per capability (model, lights, IBL, animation, picking), fixture-driven, usable for visual regression — the storybook policy applied to 3D. hexdocs wiring + sidebar groups.
notes: Scope addition: a perf stress scene in the catalog — N animated entities scalable until frame-time readback degrades, run on the weakest pool device. Turn-based consumers (Chopaat) never stress the frame loop; this scene is what keeps the 60fps claim honest. Pairs with the frame-time introspection in mob_scene3d-0n7.

title: Camera control helpers: orbit / pan / zoom
description: Optional Elixir-side camera controllers (orbit around target, pan, pinch zoom) built on the input events — app code opts in per scene. Pure Elixir over the IR; no native changes expected.

title: glTF animation playback
description: Play/pause/seek named glTF animations via the IR (gltfio Animator on the native side); animation state readable through scene readback so agents can assert playback. Recording-based device acceptance (stills prove nothing about motion).
notes:
Validating use case (Chopaat cowrie throws): support selecting among multiple named animations baked into one .glb — the pattern is rules-engine rolls first, runtime plays a randomly-chosen baked tumble matching the outcome (animations generated agentically via Blender headless rigid-body sim → keyframe bake → glTF export). Requirements this implies: fast animation selection by name, an on-complete event to the screen process ({:animation_done, id}), and post-settle scene/1 readback exposing entity orientations so a driving agent can assert the visual outcome matches the rolled value. No runtime physics — that stays out of scope deliberately.
MERGED after independent test re-run + security-flag review: the chopaat tumble fixtures (tumbles.glb + manifest) committed into s3d_spike/priv as acceptance material were ALREADY public on GenericJam/chopaat master (same owner, both repos public) — no exposure; provenance = chopaat feat/tumble-library. If chopaat ever goes private, remove/regenerate these fixtures. k0/k4/k7 manifest contract verified identically on emulator + iOS sim + physical Moto; 132 host tests; loop/seek/replay/unknown all honest.

comments.author: GenericJam
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED + device-verified on branch feat/animation (HEAD 046bf1b; feat commit 7d3437f). Master untouched.

API shape: %Animation{name, play_id, loop, speed, paused, seek} drives gltfio Animator on the render thread; replay = play_id change; on_animation_done: tag on the viewport (default :animation_done -> delivers {:animation_done, play_id} tuple as-is, pick-tag grammar; ruled in decisions/2026-08-30-animation-playback.md). scene/1 gains per-model animation_state (name/play_id/time/done/paused/loop, or unknown_animation error marker) + nodes (named glTF node world transforms) — the settle-readback surface. set_animation added to both native caps; wire schema STAYS 1 (additive op per the versioning rule — a bump would break old-Elixir/new-native for no reason); skew host-tested ({:unsupported, :set_animation} against pre-animation caps). Unknown clip: SYNC {:unknown_animation, id, name} once the render thread registers the asset clip list; async scene3d_error when racing the load. Completion needs a running clock (paused seek-to-end holds pose, no event); done at most once per play_id; dt clamped 100ms so background pause never fast-forwards.

CHOPAAT CONTRACT — full pass on ALL THREE targets (evidence/{android_emu,ios_sim,android_moto}_animation_battery.txt; values are the evidence): tumbles.glb loaded, throw_k0_v0/throw_k4_v0/throw_k7_v0 played :once, {:animation_done, play_id} observed ~1.5-2.6s, seven shell slot orientations read via scene/1 nodes, classified with tumble.py rule (local +Y world-Y <= -0.7): 0/4/7 up exactly, per-slot arrays == manifest on emulator (buildpool1), pool-ios-0 sim, and physical Moto ZY22DP6HFL. k4 per-slot components crisp on all targets (settled |dot| ~0.99-1.0, nothing near the 0.7 band). Loop: clock advances, no done, Moto sustained 60fps under playback (76 frames/1.2s, avg 16.707ms, 0 dropped). Seek+paused: t held exactly (readback 0.05/1.5), node travel 3-7cm between poses, sample_region distinguishes. Replay re-fires. Unknown name errors sync. Mid-tumble compositor caps + Moto screenrecord committed.

Gates all green: format, credo --strict (0), warnings-as-errors, 132 host tests, erlfmt, clang-format, ktlint, swiftlint. Apps uninstalled from all three devices; moto/ios-sim/buildpool leases released (client s3d-anim@build).

Notes for future lanes: (1) iOS needed an explicit NameComponentManager in AssetConfiguration for instance-node names — Android's AAR wires one implicitly. (2) mob.deploy pushes iOS-sim runtime per MOB_SIM_RUNTIME_DIR (not SIMCTL_CHILD_-prefixed) — mismatch = boot loop; launch the app with SIMCTL_CHILD_MOB_SIM_RUNTIME_DIR pointing at the SAME root the deploy used. (3) Physical iPhone still unverified (same t05 gap); the animation driver is platform-shared with the sim-verified Metal path.

title: Runtime physics: embed Jolt for live rigid-body simulation
description: Owner interest (2026-08-31): real physics in the game — animations built on the fly instead of baked. Feasible: Jolt Physics (MIT, C++, mobile-proven) embeds exactly like Filament did (prebuilt libs both platforms — the spike playbook + the mob_dev #55 manifest work apply directly). Architecture: physics runs on its own fixed-timestep thread (or the render thread's tick), bodies map to IR entities, transforms flow physics→Filament per frame; IR gains a physics surface (body: static|dynamic|kinematic, shape refs — convex hulls from the asset pipeline, impulses, gravity, a sleep/settled event). FAIRNESS DECISION (recorded now, binding on consumers): live physics provides FEEL, rules provide TRUTH — for outcome-bearing throws the sim runs live but the final ~0.3s blends to a pose matching the rules-drawn outcome (the bake script's smoothstep trick moved to runtime); pure-physics outcomes are OFF the table for anything fair-play-relevant because cross-platform float determinism is unreliable and it breaks server authority for future online. The baked library remains the fallback tier and the verification ground truth (a live tumble's settled orientations must satisfy the same classifier). Introspection is a feature gate per AGENTS.md: body states readable, settled events honest, frame_stats extended with physics-step timing. Phase it: (1) embedding spike (both platforms, size/build-cost answers, determinism characterization), (2) IR physics surface + applier, (3) the guided-settle throw as the validating consumer (chopaat shake-to-throw), (4) parity/perf harness extension. Do not start before the game ships v1 unless the owner promotes it.
notes:
Architecture ruling (owner discussion, 2026-08-31): TARGET = separate plugin (mob_physics3d) — renderer-without-physics is the common case and nobody shipping a product viewer should pay Jolt's megabytes; ecosystem grain is small composable plugins. PATH = incubate inside mob_scene3d first: phase 1 adds the native DRIVER SEAM to scene3d (registration point where a native transform producer writes entity transforms on the render tick, pre-patch — this seam is valuable independent of physics: future IK/procedural animation plugs in the same way), phase 2 builds Jolt against that seam in-tree behind an ENFORCED internal boundary (physics code touches only the driver seam — boundary test, chopaat-xref style), repo split to mob_physics3d happens once the seam survives the guided-settle throw implementation. Deciding technical fact: the 60Hz transform handoff must be native-to-native — never through the BEAM. The seam ABI needs version-skew guards like every other native surface.
Owner ruling: nice-to-have, sequenced after gameplay is happening — P3, do not start until promoted.

title: 3D text/billboard labels
description: Games want names/values in-scene (player labels above arms, throw values above shells). Options: billboard quads with rasterized text textures (generate texture at runtime from the host's text rendering — needs a texture-upload surface, pairs with the skins bead), or SDF text. Start with billboards + host-rasterized labels; keep the API tiny (%Label{text, size, color, billboard: true}). Depends on per-instance texture support.
